title: Offline-first, EAR99-by-design structured orders, tasks, reports and LOGSTAT object layer with CRDT merge for TAK-CIV, sold first to public-safety incident command, National Guard and allied light units, with the merge model licensable to HQ planning and C2 platform owners

scores.rationale: Real but tolerated: paper ICS forms and spreadsheets work well enough that agencies keep using them; the acute failure (divergent pictures after partition) is episodic. Military-side pain is documented (Ivy Sting 4, LG-DA 2025) but that buyer is not this gap's first customer.
Every incident operational period and every Guard/allied order cycle regenerates forms and reports; disconnected multi-writer conflicts are less frequent than the form-filling itself.

HSGP $1.008B FY25 (FACT) and AFG exist but are fragmented across thousands of agencies and not evidenced for this product class; Guard has no line (Public evidence insufficient); licensing buyers unproven; DIANA EUR 100k.

Public-safety direct sales need no SBIR or ATO, which fits this cap table, but SLED buying runs on references, grant cycles and cooperative contracts with 12-24 month cycles; Guard and allied paths are pilots without a program office.
CRDT libraries, ATAK-CIV SDK and a documented mission API make it buildable; iTAK's no-plugin architecture forces a companion-app/server-side design and doubles mobile work.
PoC $80k-$150k on commercial devices and synthetic data; $250k covers PoC plus one or two exercises but not a sales function.
3-5 months to a partition-and-merge demo on five devices; a credible demo to a buyer (live exercise) adds a season.
ICS forms, doctrinal report formats and TAK schemas are public; only real Guard LOGSTAT data needs a sponsor and is not required for the first product.

Civil, open-source, plausibly EAR99 product with no clearance/ATO for public safety; not 5 because Guard/allied variants bring TAK-GOV gating, possible defense-service and CUI questions that need counsel.

Entirely unclassified by design: public-safety users, ATAK-CIV/TAK Server open builds, public schemas, commercial mesh; no CUI or classified dependency at any stage of the first product - the one criterion where this gap is unambiguously strong.

Every slice is occupied: TPC's free Data Sync (disconnect re-sync), Ditto's funded CRDT ATAK plugin (merge engine), Resgrid/Tablet Command/Intterra/WebEOC/Veoci (ICS forms, Resgrid offline-first), Onebrief/Anduril-Rivet/Systematic (military orders), plus open-source CRDTs; the DHS SAVER 2022 survey shows a mature multi-vendor IMS category.

TPC can add form objects to missions, Ditto can ship a schema pack, IMS vendors can add multi-writer merge; none is locked into an architecture that prevents it. Slight vulnerability only because none currently combines all three and public-safety vendors are slow.

ATAK-CIV plugin SDK and TAK Server mission API are open and documented; iTAK is closed to plugins, TAK-GOV/MIL gated, and every military HQ platform API (Onebrief, Lattice, SitaWare) is incumbent-controlled.

CRDT merge is commoditized (Automerge, Yjs, Ditto), the schemas are public NIMS/FM standards, TAK is free government software and switching cost for an agency is near zero; the only conceivable moat (de facto community schema plus installed base) is a standards/community outcome, not proprietary.
Genuinely dual-use core (ICS forms and military orders/LOGSTAT share the object-and-merge engine) and both communities already use TAK; not 5 because both markets are small and fragmented.

Expansion from public safety into the Guard/Army layer runs into the same incumbents that killed G18/G06; the 'license the merge model' expansion is refuted by commoditization; adjacent IMS features would just make it another IMS vendor.
Per-agency SaaS subscriptions renew annually and grant cycles recur, but ACVs are small (low five figures) and churn to free TAK Data Sync or an incumbent IMS is easy.

Better than the parents: no SBIR, no CUI, non-U.S.-person founder unconstrained on an EAR99/open-source civil product, engineer can build the core. Still 2 because the team lacks the fatal-if-absent incident-command/fire-service domain founder and any SLED sales experience, and the founders' stated goal is the U.S. defense market, which this gap abandons.

market.summary: No budget owner: public-safety money is HSGP/AFG/local budgets spread over thousands of agencies with no evidence of purchases in this product class; the Guard has no program office or line for a battalion orders/reports app (Public evidence insufficient); allied entry is EUR 100k DIANA grants (2027 window closed 2026-07-03) and CIHBw pilots; the 'license the merge model' revenue line has no evidenced buyer and competes with open-source CRDTs and Ditto. TAK Public Safety's own charter says adoption is gated by training, not features. Even a successful outcome is a low-ACV niche SaaS or acquihire - consultancy/feature drift is the base case.

competition.summary: Each component already has an owner: TPC's free Data Sync re-syncs missions after disconnect and TPC could add form objects; Ditto (~$136M) sells CRDT sync for ATAK and claims USSOCOM use; Resgrid IC already markets offline-first ICS-201 and Tablet Command/Intterra/WebEOC/Veoci own agency IMS relationships (DHS SAVER 2022); Onebrief/Anduril-Rivet/Systematic hold the military orders layer. Open-source CRDT libraries and the FreeTAKTeam/Meshtastic community can replicate the rest. Switching cost is near zero and the interfaces that matter (iTAK, TAK-GOV, Onebrief/Lattice/SitaWare APIs) are controlled by others.

feasibility.summary: Not refuted: the product is unclassified, buildable for under $150k on commercial devices with public schemas, needs no ATO/CUI/SBIR for its first customers, and the non-U.S.-person founder can work on an EAR99/open-source civil codebase (counsel still required). Residual weaknesses are iTAK's closed plugin model (doubles mobile work), the missing fatal-if-absent incident-command domain founder and SLED sales capability, and classification/defense-service drift if the Guard or allied variants add military-specific integration.

verdict_rationale: KILL as a venture, with an explicit note that it is a legitimate bootstrapped/open-source niche business. Applying the same standard as the parent red teams: the buyer chain exists only in its civil half (PROBLEM -> incident commander -> agency chief -> no program office -> municipal/state procurement -> HSGP/local budget -> direct SaaS sale) and is fragmented across thousands of small buyers with no evidence of purchases in this product class; the Guard half has no requirement owner, program office, budget or vehicle (Public evidence insufficient), which draws the major chain penalty for that segment; the allied half is EUR 100k grants with the 2027 DIANA window already closed. Market attractiveness is 2.7, dragged by competitive intensity (1) and moat (1): TPC's free Data Sync, Ditto's funded CRDT ATAK plugin, Resgrid's offline-first ICS-201 and the mature IMS category (DHS SAVER 2022) occupy every slice, and the 'licensable merge model' - the one piece of the thesis that could have been venture-scale - is refuted by open-source CRDTs and Ditto's existing product. Founder fit is the highest of the family at 3.8 because everything is unclassified, cheap, EAR99-plausible and needs no SBIR, so the feasibility skeptic could not refute it; but strong feasibility of a small business does not make a venture, and the founders' stated primary interest (U.S. defense) is abandoned by this form. Confidence MEDIUM: a signed multi-agency state contract, a TPC statement declining to add form objects, or evidence that Ditto/IMS vendors will not cover offline multi-writer forms would raise it to borderline.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not borderline. For the record, the only form worth keeping alive is as a non-venture: an open-source 'ICS objects for TAK' schema and TAK Server extension (ICS 201/204/209/214 as CRDT-merged mission objects, iOS/Android/web companion) stewarded with TAK Public Safety and WFTAK, monetized through hosting/support to state wildland agencies and IMTs - a lifestyle/open-source business or a path to an acquihire by Ditto, a TPC contractor or an IMS vendor, with the Guard/allied and merge-model-licensing lines dropped.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today and insisted on G34, the first build is a TAK Server extension plus ATAK-CIV plugin plus a thin iOS/web companion that stores ICS 204 assignments, ICS 209/214 status and a LOGSTAT-style resource ledger as CRDT-merged mission objects, transported as compact deltas over Meshtastic/goTenna/FirstNet - about $100k and four months, entirely unclassified and buildable by the non-U.S.-person founder. They would show it to a state wildland fire technology lead running WFTAK, a Type 2 IMT planning section chief, the TAK Public Safety community and one Guard battalion S3 on a drill weekend; the demo proves that six hours of disconnected multi-writer edits to assignments and quantities merge with zero re-keying on both Android and iOS, and that the next operational period's ICS 204s are produced faster than on paper. The customer cares because forms are re-keyed every period and pictures diverge after every displacement. But an incumbent can crush it: TPC can add form objects to its free Data Sync missions, Ditto already sells CRDT sync for ATAK, Resgrid already markets offline-first ICS-201, and Tablet Command/Intterra own the agency relationships; the schema is a public standard and the merge engine is open source, so nothing becomes proprietary. The milestone that would justify $2-5M - twenty-plus paying agencies or a state-level enterprise contract plus a signed licensing/integration LOI from TPC, Onebrief, Ditto or Systematic - is unlikely to be reached because the licensing buyer has no reason to pay for what it can take from open source, and the agency ACVs are too small to fund a sales team. That is why it fails as a venture while remaining a reasonable open-source niche business or acquihire path.
bear_case_summary: Fragmented grant-sized public-safety budgets with no evidence of purchases in this class; no Guard program office, requirement or line; allied channel limited to EUR 100k DIANA grants (2027 window closed) and CIHBw pilots; every technical slice already occupied (TPC Data Sync, Ditto CRDT ATAK plugin, Resgrid offline ICS-201, mature IMS vendors, Onebrief/Anduril/Systematic on the military side); iTAK blocks plugins for the iOS-majority wildland users; CRDT and schemas are commodities so no moat; the licensing thesis has no evidenced buyer; team lacks a fire-service/incident-command founder and SLED sales; realistic upside is an acquihire.
bull_case_summary: Public-safety TAK use is real and growing (DHS S&T, WFTAK, TAK Public Safety 2024, FirstNet-paired municipal use 2025), cheap mesh has made disconnected multi-node operation routine, the product is unclassified, EAR99-plausible, buildable for ~$100k with no SBIR/ATO/CUI, the non-U.S.-person founder is unconstrained, NATO DIANA's 2027 challenges name almost exactly this problem, no one has yet combined structured ICS/orders objects with multi-writer merge inside TAK, and an installed base plus a de facto TAK ICS-object schema could make the team an attractive acquihire for Ditto, a TPC contractor, Onebrief or an IMS vendor.
